review_text: Trust me, the Spanish Latte Cold Brew is a must try. Also liked their cream puff. It was a quick stop but worth it. Will definitely check out other items on the menu next time. Service was also great, despite a busy time. Keep it up

Staff are always in a rush even during slow hours. 3 out of the 4 times I ordered in person (3 dine-in, 1 take-out) the one who took my order seemed like they were in a rush. my first 2 visits, i encountered the same barista. Talked fast with a monotonous unwelcoming tone. 3rd time was a different guy. he was the most neutral, like what you'd expect from cafes. 4th and most recent visit, this was the most annoying of them all. I was ready to say my usual order, their famous spanish cold brew 16oz. When the lady behind the counter asked for my order, i said "isa pong spanish cold brew s—" then she interrupted me by saying "size po?" even tho i was about to say it. and then when i said "sixtee—" she cut me AGAIN by saying "for here or to go". After taking my order, i was told to wait for a bit for the card payment (she took orders but queued the payments) so i decided to sit down. When she called me, i stood up next to the people in line because i was only going to pay and they were still making their order. the barista then told me "one line lang po sir". me, embarrassed, went to the back of the line. the barista then looked at me and said "dito lang po sir for payment" referring to the front of the line. even the other customers looked confused with her directions. drink is good but its not worth the terrible service

Spanish cold brew is my go to but somewhat the milk has changed? I dont know if others would agree with me. Last year was so good that I had to order it several times via grab but had a little bit of pause this year’s caffeine in take. The taste changed when I ordered dine in a day ago.

I'm at a loss for words to convey how exceptional their Spanish Cold Brew beverage is. If you're in search of it, this cafe is the ultimate destination. Despite its cozy size, it's a bustling spot, frequented by many daily. The owners are incredibly involved and hospitable, and their team follows suit. They also use high-quality local coffee beans. Don't hesitate to grab your atCurbside drink and savor it with their exquisite pastries!

The place is a bit far off from the busy streets as it's located in a residential area. When we got there, there was no signage in sight to tell you that you're at the cafe. The cafe is really small inside as It can only accommodate 2 people. As for their alfresco seating, it can also only accommodate approximately five maybe six people so that's something to consider when you want to get something to drink here. In terms of their drinks, I ordered their vegan horchata since I wanted to know what horchata tastes like and as for my boyfriend, he ordered their chocolate milk. Horchata is a bit of an acquired taste, but I personally liked it. It tastes kind of like soy milk. As for the chocolate milk, I also liked it since the sweetness was balanced out by the bitter flavor of chocolate. Will try to order their coffees next time. Lastly, I recommend getting there milk cake. It's my favorite from their line of pastries! Overall, would still recommend.

Found inside an open subdivision, you can drive past this unassuming park-drop-go cafe without a clue….Signage is discreet. (Oh wait, there’s no signage, only sun shades)….The couple of Grab/Food Panda riders crossing in front helped me in a way. The Spanish Cold Brew vividly reminds me of a similar Saint Brunch latte (from Saint Brunch)….Others I sampled are the Sea Salt Cold Brew, Cream Puff, and Milk Cake— all surpassed my expectations. Truly a local pride!
Coffee and food is great. I love their Spanish cold brew. But the place is too crowded. Mostly with students as it’s near a school. Not good if you want to work or just wanna have some quiet time.
The best coffee in Davao for casual drinkers! I always bring first-time visitors to try their Cold Brew Spanish Latte, and it leaves them wanting more every single time.
Best iced coffee in the city with their Spanish cold brew. The place is quite small to dine in but the quality of their drinks is superb.

@atcurbside is a delightful surprise that I got to experience during one of my rides in my hometown. The street is quite serendipitous for me as it was where I had spent most of my childhood years, and you bet this place now holds a special spot in my heart. Verdict 🍰All of their pastries are incredibly delicious, and I'm not even a cake person! I love their Mango Charlotte and Milk Cake. You'd think they're super sweet, but are actually balanced in taste and serving size. (But tbh, I could eat a whole Milk Cake by myself) ☕I've only ever tried their Spanish Cold Brew Latte (for the coffee-based drinks) and as they put it, it's a good introductory caffeinated drink for people who are new to coffee. It is quite refreshing and has enough caffeine to get me through the day. 🍵Their homemade tea is just as refreshing. Cleanses your palate well while enjoying all the cakes and quesadillas. 🍕Their beef quesadilla is not heavily marinated with powdered mixes and spices, it tastes just right. I love how each bite doesn't come with any guilt. 🍨Their affogato is a perfect cold dessert, with the nuttiness of the coffee blending well with their ice cream. I am a fan. Apart from the location and food, the owners (who run the entire place), are accommodating and friendly. You can get a sense of their pride and passion, in the work that they do, with their scrumptious food and refreshing drinks you They don't exactly have any parking space, nor bike racks, but you can park at your own risk (which isn't that risky really, lol) Location: 77 Topaz St., Marfori, Davao City They also have pop-ups at Woodridge Gate 2, Ma-a on Wednesdays and Saturdays (But best to always check their IG page for announcements, in case of changes with their schedule) P.S. I chanced upon their pop-up in December 2021, but they were already closing then, so I ended up buying their portafilter and steaming pitcher keychains instead. :D

Go-to coffee shop and go-to coffee. Dami ko nang nabudol sa Spanish Cold Brew nila haha. For someone who likes their coffee milky and not bitter, it’s perfect for me. There’s really something about the milk that’s just so addictive. The staff are very friendly and the place can seat about 10 people in total as they also have chairs outside.
the recipe for the spanish cold brew changed, it is way too sweet it taste like syrup with milk

Curbside Coffee is a hidden gem that brings convenience and quality together. The coffee itself is exceptional, with a range of flavorful brews that cater to all tastes. The friendly staff ensures that each order is prepared with care and delivered with a smile. Whether you're in a rush or simply enjoy the convenience, Curbside Coffee is a must-visit for a quick and satisfying caffeine fix.
Always a fan of their spanish cold brew. Matcha was grassy and the oatmilk upgrade was a bit pricey.
The customer service was disappointing, but the coffee was excellent.

The beverages are always good - I have tried Spanish latte and matcha latte (not sweet which I like). I found the egg bap’s bread a bit dry and thick. The egg salad filling wasn’t too little, the bread was just too thick and dry and overpowered the egg filling. My son said the cheese quesadilla was good.

"At Curb Side" coffee shop is a hidden gem in Davao City! Their Spanish cold brew is a delightful blend of flavors, and the Signature milk cake is simply divine. It's the perfect spot to relax and indulge in some delicious treats. Highly recommended! ☕️🍰
The best Spanish Cold Brew I've tasted so far! but limited space.
best Spanish Cold Brew ever, actually best coffee in town
Coffee is very good. Place is very small. Good for a take out or order from Grab.

Wonderful coffee shop in my Marfori Heights. It’s a micro cafe but there’s nothing tiny about this place when it comes to coffee and their service! Exceptional customer service — T, E, & J are the best! This place is my absolute fave in the city. They’re vegan Spanish latte is a must try.

We visited around 6:42pm, even though the sandwich was available they refused to serve us because some ovens were said to be off (I don't know if it is usual practice to turn off the equipments earlier than closing time (8pm) — but at around 7pm a foreigner ordered a sandwich they turned on the oven and willing served him reheated sandwich haha. It's our first time to visit so it's sad haha. I hope they are not biased when it comes to their services. It's like they closed in a hurry since it's almost 8pm :(((

There was no rice meal served but it smelled like you ate at a greasy restaurant. It's still early. You still have a lot of walking to do but you need to go home to change clothes. It's a shame.
